definitions: A memory allocator that maintains a per-thread cache of memory blocks to reduce contention and improve performance for multi-threaded applications.
An optimization technique in memory management where each thread has its own small pool of memory to draw from, minimizing global lock contention.
examples: The Thread-Caching Allocator significantly improved the application's speed.
Implementing a Thread-Caching Allocator can reduce overhead.
Many high-performance systems utilize a Thread-Caching Allocator.
